learning: Iteration 0 drifted off the line at max error about 0.062 to 0.066 m with low oscillation, so the limit is steering authority, not damping. The kp and kd changes test that, and the next race will show whether geometry or controller gain was the bottleneck.
notes: Complete package for the Builder's iteration 1 geometry: narrower 0.10 m track and lighter body, with the controller raised to kp 4.5 and kd 0.3 to supply the extra turn authority that iteration 0 lacked. base_speed is trimmed to 1.4 to give steering more time per bend.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced 60 trials with none finishing. All 60 ended off track, with mean progress 0.23 (oval), 0.14 (s-bend) and 0.10 (slalom). Max error sat at 0.062 to 0.066 m, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit, while steering oscillation stayed low (about 0.13 to 0.15). The failure is the robot drifting off the line on bends, not jitter, so the controller needs more steering authority, not more damping. I adopt the Builder's entity0 geometry as proposed: wheel_track 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg, body_length 0.14 m, sensors at y = 0.06 m, sensor_size 0.016 m. The narrower track and lower yaw inertia already raise turn rate, so the controller changes are kept modest: kp rises from 3.0 to 4.5 so each sensor unit gives about 50 percent more PWM differential (350 per turn unit), and kd rises from 0.2 to 0.3 to damp the faster response. base_speed drops from 1.5 to 1.4 because the robot leaves the line at its current speed before it can correct, and a slightly slower run gives the steering more time per bend. The off-track limit is 0.06 m for this body width, so I keep body_width at 0.12 m. The 16 mm footprint widens the tape-visible band, and the linear weights (+1, +0.5, 0, -0.5, -1) still match the sensor x positions. ki stays at 0 to avoid windup on bends. Expected result: fewer off-track ends and more progress on the slalom and s-bend. This is a prediction, not a measurement. The controller changes are not separable from the geometry changes in this race, so the next race is the test.
